back: Starter pools give near-instant sessions with fixed sizing. Custom pools let you choose node family, size, and autoscale range at the cost of start-up time. Keyword: start-up.
Several notebooks share one Spark session, so the second and third notebook skip session start-up entirely. Keyword: shared session.
Group workspaces into a data mesh with their own admins, branding, and default sensitivity labels — a discovery and governance construct, not a security boundary. Keyword: data mesh.
Commit pushes workspace changes to the branch; update pulls branch changes into the workspace. Two-way, per workspace. Keyword: commit vs update.
Rebind a data source or parameter per stage, so a model promoted to production points at the production warehouse. Without them a deployment carries dev connections forward. Keyword: rebind.
Complementary, not alternatives: git is source of truth and review, pipelines are the promotion mechanism between stage workspaces. Keyword: review vs promote.
Viewer reads data. Contributor creates and edits items. Member also shares and adds members. Admin manages and deletes the workspace. Keyword: Contributor can edit.
Read sees the item and its endpoint. ReadData queries through SQL. ReadAll reads the underlying OneLake files. Read alone queries nothing. Keyword: which surface.
Obscures the displayed value — default, email, random, or custom mask — without restricting access. UNMASK permission reveals the real value. Keyword: obscure, not deny.

front: Why SQL RLS is not enough
back: A policy on the SQL analytics endpoint governs T-SQL only. A Spark notebook reading the Delta files directly bypasses it. OneLake security closes the gap. Keyword: which engine enforces.
Column-level hides specific columns of a table. Object-level hides the whole table or view. Keyword: granularity.
A label on a lakehouse flows downstream to models and reports built from it, and travels with exports to Excel or PDF. Keyword: downstream and outward.
Promoted (anyone with write access), Certified (authorised reviewers), Master data (the authoritative source). None of them change permissions. Keyword: discovery signal.

front: Dataflow Gen2 vs notebook vs pipeline
back: Dataflow for low-code Power Query. Notebook for code and scale. Pipeline to orchestrate and copy at volume, calling the other two. Keyword: which job.
An Activator or Reflex item watches for an event — a file landing in OneLake — and starts a pipeline. The answer to 'when a file arrives' rather than 'every hour'. Keyword: Activator.
Parameters plus dynamic expressions turn one pipeline into a loop over a control table of many tables, instead of one pipeline per table. Keyword: parameterise.
Hold warehouse schema as code so it can be built, diffed, and deployed like application source. Keyword: schema as code.
Record item creation, access, permission changes, and exports; surfaced through Purview compliance and the admin monitoring workspace. Keyword: who accessed what.
Store the last high value of a modified timestamp, filter the source above it, and write the new high value on success. Keyword: control table.
Updates matching rows and inserts new ones in one statement — the upsert that makes an incremental load correct rather than duplicating. Keyword: upsert.
Type 1 overwrites the attribute and loses history. Type 2 closes the current row with an end date and inserts a new current row. Keyword: keep history?
If the scenario needs INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE through T-SQL, the answer is a Warehouse, not a Lakehouse. Keyword: writes need a Warehouse.
High-volume time-series and telemetry queried with KQL. Not the store for a dimensional model. Keyword: time-series.
Operational and transactional workloads, not analytics — distinct from the Warehouse, which is the analytical T-SQL engine. Keyword: OLTP.
A pointer to data elsewhere — another workspace, ADLS Gen2, S3, GCS, Dataverse. One copy, no refresh, and the source's own permissions still apply. Keyword: zero copy.

front: Shortcut works for me, fails for them
back: A shortcut resolves with the caller's credentials against the target. The analyst lacks access to the underlying storage. Keyword: caller's credentials.
Continuously replicates a live operational database — Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Snowflake — into OneLake as Delta, near real time, with no ETL to write. Keyword: replicate a database.
Shortcut when the data already sits in a lake you can point at. Mirroring when the source is a live operational database. Keyword: lake vs database.
A window function ranked by an ordering column, keeping rank 1 — dropDuplicates cannot choose which copy to keep. Keyword: keep the newest.
Insert an inferred member — a placeholder dimension row filled in later — or reprocess a trailing window so the fact finds its key. Keyword: inferred member.
Eventstream is low-code with an event-processing editor. Structured streaming is code with checkpointing and exactly-once, for arbitrary logic. Keyword: low-code vs code.
Transforms data as it lands in an Eventhouse table — the right choice when the data is already arriving there. Keyword: transform on ingest.
Caches shortcut data for faster Real-Time Intelligence queries at a storage cost. Between a native table and a plain shortcut. Keyword: cached shortcut.
Tumbling is fixed-size and non-overlapping — every event in one window. Hopping advances by a smaller hop and overlaps — the moving average. Keyword: overlap.
Groups events separated by less than a timeout and closes when the gap exceeds it — how activity becomes a user session. Keyword: gap timeout.
Event time is when it happened, in the payload. Processing time is when the system saw it. Window on event time or network delay moves events into the wrong bucket. Keyword: which clock.
One view of pipeline runs, dataflow refreshes, Spark applications, and model refreshes, filterable by item, status, and time. Keyword: all runs.
Shows compute usage against the capacity — where throttling and smoothing are diagnosed when everything is slow rather than broken. Keyword: throttling.
Alerts on the meaning of the data — watches a stream, KQL query, or Power BI visual and triggers an action when a condition holds. Keyword: data condition.

front: Pipeline built a wrong file path
back: Inspect the activity's resolved input in the run detail — a dynamic expression that produced the wrong string is invisible in the definition. Keyword: resolved input.
Do not fail the refresh; they land in the query's error rows, which is where a type conversion failure on a few rows appears. Keyword: error rows.
Writes intermediate results to the lakehouse — enabling it can rescue a memory failure; disabling it for a simple query removes a needless write. Keyword: memory lever.
Someone called collect or toPandas on a large DataFrame and pulled it back to one machine. Executor OOM is skew or oversized partitions. Keyword: which JVM.
One task still running long after the others finished, visible in the Spark UI. Fix by salting the key or letting adaptive query execution coalesce. Keyword: one slow task.
Compacts many small files into fewer large ones — the first answer to a table that has slowed as appends accumulated. Keyword: small files.
V-Order is Fabric's write-time Parquet encoding, on by default. Z-Order clusters by chosen columns so filters skip more files. Keyword: default vs chosen.
Removes files no longer referenced, reclaiming storage after compaction. Its retention period must be respected or time travel breaks. Keyword: reclaim.
Partitioning by a high-cardinality column produces the small-file problem it was meant to solve. Partition on moderate cardinality that is actually filtered on. Keyword: cardinality.
Sends a small table to every executor and eliminates the shuffle — the biggest single win joining a large fact to a small dimension. Keyword: no shuffle.
Decides how much data stays on hot SSD. A hot cache shorter than the queries reach is what makes a KQL dashboard slow. Keyword: hot cache.
